issues.claim: Logging filters watch for changes through `IOptionsMonitor<LoggerFilterOptions>`, so the new rule takes effect at once if the configuration source reloads
issues.problem: This is the central 'apply without a redeploy' claim, and neither fetched excerpt shows it. The logging excerpt covers default level, filter functions and scopes. The configuration-providers excerpt only shows `reloadOnChange: true` for JSON files. The claim matches my recollection of Microsoft.Extensions.Logging (LoggerFactory refreshes filters on LoggerFilterOptions changes, and AddConfiguration registers a change token source), but the cited pages do not confirm it here. The same applies to 'the default host adds appsettings.json with reloadOnChange: true': the excerpt shows an explicit AddJsonFile call, not the default host.
issues.suggestedFix: Confirm against the logging docs, or against the Microsoft.Extensions.Logging source, that changes to the Logging configuration section are picked up at runtime. Then either cite the exact doc page that says so, or soften to 'the logging configuration section is reloaded when its configuration source reloads'. Keep the IOptionsMonitor detail only if it is confirmed.

issues.claim: For each provider the rule with the longest matching category prefix is chosen
issues.problem: The statement is correct, but a provider-specific section such as `Logging:Console:LogLevel` takes precedence over the general `Logging:LogLevel` section. A candidate could set the rule in `Logging:LogLevel` and see no effect if the Console section already defines a rule for that category or for Default.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a short note: if the provider-specific section (for example `Logging:Console:LogLevel`) matches the category, put the rule there or check that it does not override it.

issues.problem: A mounted volume reloads unreliably in some environments. A Kubernetes ConfigMap mounted with subPath is not updated, and FileSystemWatcher can miss symlink swaps. The answer mentions the option without this caveat, so it reads as always working. The same applies to the EN text.
issues.suggestedFix: Add 'проверьте, что файловый наблюдатель действительно видит изменение (в Kubernetes ConfigMap с subPath не обновляется; может помочь DOTNET_USE_POLLING_FILE_WATCHER)' and the equivalent sentence in EN.

issues.claim: Метрики DORA подобраны парами: время выполнения изменений и частота развёртываний описывают скорость, доля неудачных изменений и время восстановления описывают стабильность.
issues.problem: The fetched DORA page (redirected to dora.dev/guides/dora-metrics/) says 'these five metrics' and lists a fifth one (rework rate). The question presents exactly four metrics, links the old 'four keys' URL, and calls them 'DORA metrics', so a candidate would learn an outdated model. The current guide also groups the metrics differently from the classic pairing (recovery time under throughput, change fail rate and rework rate under instability). The excerpt does not show that grouping, so it needs checking against the page.
issues.suggestedFix: Check the grouping on the current dora.dev page. Then either state 'the four classic DORA metrics' and note that the current guide adds a fifth, deployment rework rate, or rewrite the pairing as in the current guide. Replace the 'four keys' link title with the actual page title.

issues.claim: исследования DORA показывают, что скорость и стабильность улучшаются вместе, а не за счёт друг друга
issues.problem: The excerpt shows only a Farley quote ('the real trade-off ... is between better software faster and worse software slower') and the advice that smaller batches make delivery fast and stable. It does not state this research finding explicitly, though it is broadly supported.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften to 'DORA recommends reducing batch size to make delivery both fast and stable', which the page supports.
